findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row. That happens for a user who was emailed through category watching, mailing-list mode or a mention but never visited the topic. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 on the unsubscribe link from the email. Use `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row if it is missing, or handle the nil case explicitly.

findings.title: Unsubscribe toggle is not idempotent; a reload or link prefetch mutes the topic
findings.body: The action sets the level to `regular` if the user was tracking or watching, otherwise to `muted`. Hitting the same URL a second time therefore escalates from regular to muted. Browser reload, back/forward, a mail client or security scanner prefetching the link, or clicking the email link twice all re-run the GET. The user ends up with the topic fully muted, while the page text still says only 'You will stop receiving notifications'. The action should be deterministic for a given URL, for example always mute or take an explicit target level, and should not depend on the previous state.

findings.title: State-changing operation performed on a GET request
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is routed as a GET and calls `tu.save!`, so it changes the user's notification level with no CSRF token and no confirmation. Any cross-site GET, such as an image or link that targets `/t/:id/unsubscribe` while the victim is logged in, silently downgrades or mutes that topic for them. Email link scanners that auto-follow URLs trigger it too. The GET should only render the page, and the change should be a POST/PUT, which is what the client's notification button already uses (`set_notifications`).

findings.title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change and leaves reason/timestamp stale
findings.body: The level is assigned and saved directly on the model instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` is not updated and `notifications_reason_id` keeps its old value (for example `auto_watch_category`). The user's change is not recorded as `user_changed`, which later auto-tracking logic keys off (`notifications_reason_id` is null). No MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published, so other open tabs and the notification button keep the old level. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking other add_unsubscribe_link callers
findings.body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`. Any other caller, including plugins and the existing builder spec that had to be patched, raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and the email fails to send. The builder should only add the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present, or use a separate locale key.

findings.title: New unsubscribe feature has almost no test coverage
findings.body: The only test change adds `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder spec so it stops raising. Nothing asserts that the generated body or HTML contains the per-topic URL. There is no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: the slug redirect, the tracking/watching to regular and regular to muted transitions, the missing TopicUser row, and the logged-out case. There is no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url` or the new routes. The nil-TopicUser crash and the non-idempotent toggle would have been caught by such tests.

findings.title: Logged-out email recipients get a bare 403 instead of a login path
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` list, but it is the target of a link in an email. Recipients are often not logged in on the device where they open it. For a non-XHR GET the user lands on a generic 403 page with no redirect to login and no way to complete the unsubscribe, so the feature's main entry point fails for them.
